items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Franc Williams. The mention of Franc Williams occurs in the interviewer's prose note ('PS: Maybe we should ask Franc Williams...'), not in the interviewee's speech.

ctx.x: faults, I mean, that is bad for me too, you know. I don't stay in contact enough, 'cause they were a great gang, that gang. If I'd stayed in contact I could tell you more, see. Or I know that [ ] was from Buffalo, New York. And Bill - where he was born I don't know, but he came up 'round Philadelphia, see. And Ruth Marsee [?] the girl also came up 'round Phil, so where they born, I don't know. And Charlie Miller, see, in the end he turned out to be the president of an Albany musicians' local, negro - at the end,…
PS: Maybe we should ask Franc Williams, who spent some time in Albany in the '30s, if he knows Charlie Miller -
He should, yeah - yeah, yeah. Charlie Miller, that's the name. That's obviously Charlie Miller's name.
